newsitem.title: CHINA: China navy's shots in the dark hit right on target.
newsitem.headline: China navy's shots in the dark hit right on target.

text.p: A group of Chinese warships that recently held night target practice in the East China Sea found they hit more targets in the dark than in daylight firing tests, the Press Digest said on Thursday.
Live-fire night exercises by a group of destroyers from the East China Sea fleet had for the first time scored more hits than they did in similar tests held during the daytime, the newspaper said.
"This was an historic first for naval warship cannon attacks," it said.
A separate report in the army's official Liberation Army Daily said a group of reconnaissance troops recently held exercises near Taihang mountain range to the west of Beijing.

The drills appeared to be commando-style in nature, with troops carrying out hostage rescue and armed reconnaissance manoeuvres, said the October 2 edition of the newspaper available in Beijing on Thursday.
"Nowadays they concentrate the land, water and air reserve capabilities into one... becoming a sharp knife of our army under the conditions of a high-technology war," it said.
China has carried out several high-profile military tests in recent weeks, following a flare up of a dispute over a group of contested islands in the East China Sea.
